releases.name: Anka 1.0.1
releases.body:
**Anka 1.0.1** opens games stored as **.nup** packages.

Built from [`anka`](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/tree/anka) at `2d17a71ff0f0cf0c27b3d7207818fade9199b77b`; both programs carry this commit.

## Updating from 1.0.0

Close Anka, unzip **`Anka-1.0.1-win64.zip`** into your Anka folder and replace the files. Your `user` folder (settings, keys, firmware and saves) stays as it is.

New to Anka: follow the quick start in the [1.0.0 notes](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/releases/tag/anka-v1.0.0). Unzip into a new, empty folder, start `anka.exe`, and install your own keys and firmware.

## What's in 1.0.1

### .nup packages
- `.nup` ("Unencrypted (Archival) Package") is a container format from upstream Eglantine. It holds one title's base game, update and add-on content in a single file.
- Anka now **reads** .nup files. You can open them with **File › Load File…**, and they appear in the game list with their icon, name and version. `anka-cli.exe` and its launchers open them too, including from the `Games` folder.
- Mods (LayeredFS) and Anka's game-specific settings apply to games opened from a .nup, the same as for other formats. Anka finds the title ID before the game starts.

releases.name: Anka 1.0.0
releases.body:
First release of **Anka**, a Nintendo Switch 2 emulator for Windows, focused on performance.

Built from [`anka`](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/tree/anka) at `b7542ece8b5c695e2f01d5e46b74c0806d48ae96`; both programs carry this commit.

## Quick start

1. Unzip **`Anka-1.0.0-win64.zip`** into a **new, empty folder**. Do not unzip it into another emulator's folder: its Qt DLLs would replace that program's.
2. Start **`anka.exe`**. Anka keeps its settings, keys, firmware and saves in the `user` folder next to it (portable mode) and does not touch `%APPDATA%\eden` or other installs.
3. Install your own keys and firmware as with other Eden-based emulators. Anka includes no games, keys or firmware; only use what you legally own.
4. Settings: **Emulation › Configure… › Anka**. The first start picks *Recommended*, the setup we measured (with GPU Mode *Fast*, the default; it also turns Reactive Flushing off).

Coming from PokeDinner-Eglantine 2.0.0: back up its `nand` folder (your saves), then copy its `user` folder next to `anka.exe`.

Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with a current Vulkan driver. Qt and the Visual C++ runtime come with Anka.

Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64.AppImage, for 4K, 16K and 64K page kernels alike
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

- Lower CPU load during races. Vulkan reuses uploaded vertex data, shader parameters, and descriptor sets. Index data is written directly into the rendering buffer, eliminating an intermediate copy.

- Lower audio processing overhead. The low-pass filter processes both channels in parallel, and diagnostic calculations run less often.
- Improved 30/60 FPS switching. The selected mode is applied through D3D frame presentation while preserving simulation speed and game timers.

releases.name: Copperline 1.2.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.2.0 is the second feature release of the 1.x series. It adds a video slot with an emulated NewTek Video Toaster 4000 and Video Flyer, an Amiga 2000 profile, a terminal display that also works over SSH, single-file web pages for floppy titles, high-density floppies and MP4 recording. The CPU core gains a long list of conformance fixes, and Copper, sprite, beam-counter and interrupt timing are corrected. It also includes every fix made on the 1.x branch since 1.1.0.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.2.0.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version.

releases.name: Copperline 1.1.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.1.0 is the first feature release of the 1.x series. Hard drives can now run at the speed of the period drives each Amiga shipped with. The MMU-less 68EC030, 68EC040 and 68EC060 are new CPU choices. The JIT is much faster on fast-RAM code and heavy disk I/O, and has a new "fastest" speed. A500 CIA, interrupt and bus timing are corrected against measurements of a real A500. It also includes every fix made on the 1.x branch since 1.0.1.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.1.0.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version.
- **Desktop save states from 1.0.x still load.** The CIA chunks are migrated to their new layout. A resumed 1.0.x state continues under the corrected timing, so it can drift from what 1.0.x would have produced (a factory A500 state from 1.0.1 still renders byte-identical frames). States saved by 1.1.0 do not load in 1.0.x, which reports that the state comes from a newer Copperline.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.1
releases.body:
Copperline 1.0.1 is the first maintenance release for 1.0. Most of it fixes problems reported against 1.0.0: an AGA display fetch error, a blitter race on fast CPUs, warm reboots on the A3000 and A4000, the 68060 FPU at reset, the copperhf hard-disk driver, and a window-resize hang on Windows. Menu settings are now remembered between launches, and screenshots save the picture as you see it.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.0.1.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version. Desktop `.clstate` files still load: the save-state format has not changed, and a 1.0.0 state resumes byte-for-byte as it does in 1.0.0.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.0.0 is the first stable release. It follows two weeks of testing of 1.0.0-rc.1 and is the 23rd release since the source went public on 14 June.

This release adds Smart framing and native 1:1 screenshots, more control over where and how the window opens, VHD hard-disk images, a fix for AGA sprites that use scan-doubling, and a Check for updates button that only contacts GitHub when you press it.

## Copperline 1.0 at a glance

- **Machines:** A1000, A500, A500+, A600, A1200, A3000, A4000, CDTV and CD32, with OCS, ECS and AGA chipsets and 68000 to 68060 CPUs, FPUs and MMUs.
- **Accuracy:** the CPU and custom chips run on one colour-clock timeline, with the chip bus shared out cycle by cycle. Timing is checked against a real A1200, A4000 and CD32, and 45 test programs are compared pixel for pixel on every change.
- **Ready to run:** the open AROS ROM is bundled, as are ROMs for the A2091, A4091 and IDE boards, the CD32 FMV module and the HRTMon freezer. WHDLoad packages and Amiga programs boot directly.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.0-rc.1: the first release candidate for 1.0
releases.body:
This is the first release candidate for Copperline 1.0. If testing does not turn up problems that need a second candidate, the next release will be 1.0.0.

This cycle brings three- and four-player netplay on the desktop, debugger watchpoints on device registers with a timed trace of CD32 drive commands, a refreshed AROS ROM, and a review of the whole manual against the program, which also found and fixed a few mismatches in the program itself.

Please try your usual games, demos and configurations with it. Anything that worked in 0.21.0 and does not work here is exactly what a release candidate is for: [open an issue](https://github.com/CopperlineHQ/Copperline/issues) with the configuration and the software involved.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.0.0-rc.1.** The wire protocol moved to version 3 to carry up to four players, so a 0.21.0 peer cannot join.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version. Desktop `.clstate` files from 0.20.0 and 0.21.0 still load; states from 0.19 and earlier do not.

releases.name: v0.1.14
releases.body:
Smoother frame pacing, fewer hitches, a new frame counter.

## English

**Improvements**
- Less work per frame on the CPU side: the Vulkan commands are now recorded on a separate thread.
- Fewer missing objects or flicker for a moment while a new effect or area is seen for the first time.
- With the frame rate limit at 30, the screen switches to 60 Hz, so frames come out evenly. The limit in the ⚙ menu now applies right away, without a restart.
- The GPU clock is kept from dropping too low while frames run late, and the GPU work is handed over more evenly.
- Better rendering with the phone's own (system) Vulkan driver on Adreno.
- The frame counter is now a small separate overlay with a dot that shows when the phone is getting hot and slowing down. Long-press the counter to see what the dot means.
- More detail in the log if the graphics driver crashes, to help fix such reports.

releases.body:
Changes since the latest beta release:
- Fixed two UI issues (#843, #846)
- Fixed a bug in the CBM file system implementation (#853)
- Fixed a bug in the drive idle logic (#854)
- Fixed three drive-related VICE tests (#668, #674, #675)

Core and API

* Public API: The API now has as new shape. There are async counterparts (…Async) for state-changing calls, set is now setAsync, there is a new MemoryDebugger API, more getters, and suspend/resume coverage across the API.
* Threading: The command queue and message queue are now std::deque-based. Messages can carry exceptions. AudioPort is thread-safe. Cmd::CALL, TRACK_ON and TRACK_OFF are new.
* Messages: Msg::CONFIG is sent for every option change. ROM_LOADED, RSH_DONE and CONFIG_ERROR are new.
* RetroShell: It has the new architecture from vAmiga, with multiple shells and a single console per shell.
* Workspaces: A screenshot is now saved inside saveWorkspace().
* X-Ray: GPU X-Ray support is added, with a new XRAY_COMPOSITOR option.
* Shared libraries: utlib and rvlib were merged with the versions shared with vAmiga and Silicium.
* Cleanup: Header, include and namespace cleanups, plus removal of orphaned files.

Fixes

* Drive::isIdle() is fixed (#854).

This maintenance release primarily addresses issue #851, which prevented the app from running on the upcoming macOS 27 Golden Gate. It also includes internal code changes required to make the core compatible with the architecture of the upcoming Silicium emulator.
Removing beta status, as no significant bugs have been reported for some time.

## Refactoring

This beta release introduces substantial changes to the underlying code base. As part of the development of the RetroVault app, a new **RetroVault** library has been created. This library is now responsible for managing:

- File systems  
- Devices  
- All supported image formats  

RetroVault is designed as a standalone library and is also used in the latest version of vAmiga for the same purpose.

In addition, the new **utlib** library has been introduced. All utility functions previously embedded in vAmiga and VirtualC64 have been refactored into this more powerful shared library. This makes it easier for me to share common functionality among the different emulators. 

## Enhancements

- The disassembler now supports symbol files (#837)

## Bug Fixes

- Fixed a crash in the file system importer when importing excessively large folders (#841)  
- Fixed a bug in the VIC inspector that prevented selecting individual sprites in Tahoe (#840)

releases.name: CosmoU 0.13.0
releases.body:
## ✨ A calmer, clearer CosmoU

CosmoU 0.13 reworks the whole interface. All the features are still there, just sorted better, so every window and every theme feels like one product: easy to understand on the first start, calm with a big library, readable from the sofa.

## What changed

- **Play is always the strongest button** – in Covers, Grid, the Wii U Look and the game details. Details and the other actions are quieter.
- **Grid** – a calm banner: the cover sharp in front of its own softly blurred colours, instead of a giant pixelated picture.
- **Game details** – a smaller cover, Play first, *Add to favorites* as a quiet toggle, one line instead of four empty statistics before the first play, the tools in one row, save data and updates as simple rows.
- **Settings** – a calmer category bar (only the open category is in colour), a bigger search with its shortcut (Ctrl F / ⌘F).
- **Quick Menu** – your games first, then three clear groups: **Look**, **Sound** and **System**.
- **Theme gallery** – big cards with a preview picture of every theme.
- **Empty screens lead somewhere** – *Clear search*, *Show the library*, or the folder button of the console you're looking at.

Every fix and idea in this update came from **Eduard**, who tested CosmoU 0.12 in depth and reported everything on Discord. Thank you so much!

- **Moving with the controller flashed like a page reload** on the console home screens – now only the selection moves.

# Lumen Emu 0.1.0 build 5 for iOS and iPadOS

This preview targets ARM64 iPhones and iPads running iOS or iPadOS 17.4 or later. The IPA is intended for sideloading and local signing with AltStore Classic. Both the PS4 and PS5 cores require JIT. Installing this build and enabling JIT through AltStore Classic still need to be verified on a physical iPhone.

## Installation and JIT setup

1. [Install the IPA with AltStore Classic](https://github.com/gs-soft-it/lumen-emu/blob/main/README.md#install-the-ipa-with-altstore-classic)
2. [Enable JIT on iPhone](https://github.com/gs-soft-it/lumen-emu/blob/main/README.md#enable-jit-on-iphone)

## Core changes

- The PS4 core uses FFmpeg for AAC decoding and Mbed TLS 3.6.7 for HTTPS. Apple Security verifies certificate trust and hostnames.
- The PS5 core uses the project's SPIR-V transformations for its native Metal renderer on iOS.
- The on-device JIT component is built from StikJIT 2.0.1 and `idevice` 0.1.68 using RustCrypto and a pinned `Cargo.lock`. The separate JIT extension uses AGPLv3. Dependency provenance and license notices are in the source archive and in `Legal/stikjit` inside the IPA.

releases.name: Xenoblade DE port v0.16.1
releases.body:
## Runtime update (no visible change in this port)

This release carries a fix from the Catherine port's runtime, which both ports share.

Some games bind a block of shader constants that is shorter than what their shader actually reads. On the console the bytes just past the block are the next bytes of the game's own structure; the port was filling them with zeros. It now copies them from the game's memory up to the next 16-byte boundary and keeps zeros beyond that.

**Nothing changes in Xenoblade: its G-buffer vertex shader reads up to 368 bytes with 256 bound, and 256 is already a multiple of 16, so it keeps getting zeros — exactly as before.** Re-verified on the Flip 2 with a copy of the save: characters whole (Shulk with the Monado, the party), 30.1 fps in battle, saves untouched.

## En español

Esta versión trae un arreglo del runtime que comparte con el port de Catherine.

releases.name: Xenoblade DE port v0.16.0
releases.body:
## No more blinking objects after loading

While the game is running, each new combination of shader and render state needs a GPU pipeline. Pipelines the app has never seen are built in the background so the game doesn't freeze, and until one is ready the objects that use it are not drawn. Until now that also happened to pipelines it had already built in an earlier session. Only the first 4,000 were prepared at start-up, in the order they first appeared, so later in the game whole areas came from the background again. The result was objects and textures blinking for a few frames after loading a save or when walking into an area.

- Pipelines that the app has already built on your device are now created on the spot, in about a quarter of a millisecond each and within a small per-frame budget, so they are drawn from the first frame.
- Start-up preparation now begins with the pipelines your last session used (`pipelines_recientes.bin` in the game folder), not with the ones from the beginning of the game.
- Areas you visit for the very first time can still show an object a moment late while its pipeline is built. The second visit is clean.

releases.name: Xenoblade DE port v0.15.0
releases.body:
## Save report and update notices

Two new rows in the settings panel (swipe in from the right edge of the screen):

- **Save report** writes a folder `reports/<date>/` into your game folder: the log, a screenshot of the moment you opened the panel, the frame times of the last seconds and basic device information (model, Android version, memory). **Nothing is sent anywhere.** If something looks wrong, open an [issue](https://github.com/IamWilmar/xenoblade-recomp/issues) and attach those files (have a look first: the log contains the names of your folders).
- **Update notices** (on by default): about eight seconds after the game starts, the app asks GitHub's public API which release is the latest. It is a single request, without an account, and nothing about you or your game is sent. If there is a newer version, a banner says so and *Get vX.Y.Z* opens its page. Switch it off in the panel (or create an empty file `sin_avisos_version` in the game folder) and the app makes no network request at all.
- Because of the update notices the app now has Android's **Internet** permission. It is used for that request only.

## Installing

releases.name: v0.14.0
releases.body:
## Sharper 3D

- **The 3D image is upscaled with AMD FSR 1 before the game adds its interface.** The game draws its 3D at a dynamic resolution (for example 704×416 in handheld mode) and stretched it to its 720p window with a simple filter; on the Flip 2 that 720p image was then stretched again to the 1080p screen. Now FSR rebuilds the 3D at 720p first, and the step to 1080p sharpens instead of only stretching. The interface is untouched. The difference is largest in TV mode, where the 3D is narrowest.
- It costs about 2.8 ms of GPU per frame and turns itself off for a moment when a heavy scene would not fit in the 30 fps frame. Measured on the Flip 2 in the open field: 30 fps in handheld and TV mode.
- To get the previous image, create an empty file named `sin_fsr_escena` in the game's data folder (it takes effect while the game runs).

## Installing

Install the APK over the previous version (your settings and saves stay) or follow the [README](https://github.com/IamWilmar/xenoblade-recomp#install-and-first-run) for a first install.

## En español

releases.name: Xenoblade DE port v0.13.0
releases.body:
## Full screen, without Android's bars

- **Android's navigation bar no longer stays on top of the game.** With three-button navigation (or a visible gesture bar) the bar at the bottom of the screen covered part of the image. The app now hides the system bars while the game runs; swipe in from an edge to bring them up for a moment. Thanks to the player who reported it on a Retroid Pocket 5; it was reproduced and checked on the Flip 2.
- The settings panel opens as before: swipe left from the right half of the screen.
- To keep the bars on screen, create an empty file named `con_barras_sistema` in the game's data folder.

releases.body:
# WWE '12 PC 1.5.0 "Small PCs"

This version is about PCs with few or slow CPU cores: a start-up freeze is fixed, parts of the game run faster, and there is a new FPS counter. It also fixes two Universe problems.

## Fixes

- **Fixed a rare freeze on "NOW LOADING" at start-up** on PCs with few or slow CPU cores (a race between the game's sound-bank loading threads). The game could stay on the first loading screen forever. On a test PC limited to 2 slow cores it froze in 2 starts out of 10 before the fix and never in 10 starts after it (#69, #74: if your freeze has another cause, tell us). 
- **No more loading-screen speed-up on PCs with fewer than 8 usable threads**, where it could lock the game at its frame barrier.
- **Universe: SmackDown (and other weekly shows) no longer end up with only 0-1 match** when their roster is small: a match that would be dropped because everyone is resting now takes a rested Superstar instead.

releases.name: WWE '12 PC 1.4.1
releases.body:
# WWE '12 PC 1.4.1

A small update after 1.4.0: a Royal Rumble crash fixed, and belt modding in the Mod Maker.

## Fixes

- **Royal Rumble crash (#79):** in 1.4.0, the animations added for the I QUIT match were loaded in **every** match. The Royal Rumble, which loads the most wrestlers, could run out of room in the game's animation memory and crash, or leave wrestlers frozen and entrants stuck behind the ramp. They are now only added in an **I QUIT** match or a **Special Guest Referee** match; every other match is the original game again. I QUIT and the special referee work as before.

## Mod Maker

- **Belt modding.** In BELTS & WEAPONS, a new **Port a belt from another game** page: bring a title belt from WWE 2K14, 2K15, WWE '13, 2K16 / 2K17 or SvR 2007-2011 in place of one of the game's belts, with its menu pictures (belt, background, statistics, unlock icons). It is a new `belt` mod type, handled by the game and the launcher. Seen in game with the 2K14 WWE title at the waist; the other games, hand and shoulder poses are less tested. You cannot add a 24th title (the save has 23): replace one you do not use.
- Updated HELP page.

## Android

releases.name: v1.4.0
releases.body:
# WWE '12 PC 1.4.0

The match-options update: new match rules in the menus (starting finishers, squash, I QUIT, Special Guest Referee), a Universe chaos level, Mod Maker additions and fixes for what you reported after 1.3.0.

## New match options

- **Starting finishers (as in WWE 2K14).** On the character select, press **LT / RT** on a place to choose how many finishers that wrestler starts with: NONE, 1, 2, 3 or INFINITE. It shows in the title of the attire frame (or in the READY banner for wrestlers with only one attire). Left on NORMAL, nothing changes. *Limit:* in a few match types the game skips the attire frame, so the option is only offered in a normal 1 on 1.
- **Squash matches.** In **OPTIONS > GAMEPLAY > BALANCING > DAMAGE** (the page now has three new lines): **SQUASH CHANCE** (0-100 %, the chance that a 1 on 1 match is a squash; 0 = off, the default), **SQUASH: JOBBER HEALTH** (starting health of the lower-rated wrestler, 20 % by default) and **STARTING FINISHERS** (default for every match). The lower-rated wrestler is the jobber; the other one starts with a finisher. The labels of the three new lines are in English only.

releases.name: v1.3.0
releases.body:
**WWE '12 PC v1.3.0 — "Speed and fixes"**

> ⚠️ No game data included: you need your own copy of WWE '12 for Xbox 360.

### Faster
- **Loading screens shorter** (a match loads in about 1.5 s instead of 4 s, the end of the entrances in about 1.9 s instead of 4.5 s). `wwe12_fast_loading = false` brings the old behaviour back.
- **Faster start-up** on PCs with 8 or more logical processors: the title screen comes after about 5-7 s instead of 15 s. On smaller processors the normal start-up is kept (`wwe12_fast_boot_min_threads`).
- **Sharper picture** when the game is drawn at 720p on a bigger screen (`svr_upscale_sharpness`, 0 turns it off).
- **Adaptive V-sync**: a late frame is shown at once instead of waiting a whole refresh (`svr_adaptive_vsync`).
- **Performance test** in the launcher (button *Performance test*): it plays a recorded 1-on-1 match with entrances once and tells you if your PC is fine, limited by the processor or by the graphics card. Nothing is changed without your agreement.

### Frame rate

**WWE '12 PC v1.2.0 — "Moveset update"**

> ⚠️ No game data included: you need your own copy of WWE '12 for Xbox 360.

### Fixed
- **Match-start stutter (and a short freeze) on integrated graphics (Intel...)**: the game's reads of the picture back from the graphics card are now grouped at the end of the frame (about 10 times less waiting at the start of a match). `svr_readback_defer_streak = false` goes back to 1.1.
- **Less work for the processor every frame** (helps small PCs, issue #53): shader constants are reused like on Android (`svr_reuse_constant_blocks`) and the check of 3D models is lighter (`svr_geometry_sample_min`, 32768 brings the 1.1 behaviour back).
- **Crash at start with file names that have accents or other characters** (for example a song called "Café.mp3" or a mod folder with Japanese letters in a mod): names are now read as UTF-8 everywhere in the game, the launcher and the Mod Maker, and a mod with an unreadable name is skipped instead of closing the game.
- **Launcher: the MUSIC page closed the launcher** when a file in the `music` folder had an odd name.

releases.body:
**Headlight beams in both games, and the first Android beta.** At night your car finally lights up the road ahead and we're releasing the Android version for further testing.

## Features

- **Headlight beams.** Turning your lights on at night now throws a beam of light onto the road ahead, as on the original Xbox: it brightens the street, cars and walls it reaches and stops where it meets them ([#10](https://github.com/laureladastra/mcdub3-nx/issues/10), thanks for the report). Before, the lights worked in the game but no beam was drawn. Other emulators (i.e. xemu → https://github.com/xemu-project/xemu/issues/996) show a solid white shape instead. The game builds the beam in a small hidden picture using two tricks of the Xbox's graphics chip that the port did not reproduce yet: it reuses a picture as a depth map, and it counts the beam's layers with a special blending mode that works with negative numbers. Both are emulated now. Tested in the DUB Edition and the Remix. The WHITE button flashes your high beams while you hold it. The main headlights are on by themselves at night.

releases.name: mcdub3-nx v1.0.0
releases.body:
**Version 1.0 for both games on the Nintendo Switch.** This release removes the last annoyances: races that felt slow when the frame rate dipped, random zoom-in or out during loading screens, and vertical lines during upscaling.

### Features

- **Races keep their real speed.** The original game moves the race forward by a fixed step every frame, which was fine on the Xbox, where it runs on a fixed 30 FPS. On the Switch, in rain, with nitrous or in the busiest streets, the frame rate can dip and the whole race then went into slow motion. The race now proceeds by the time that really passed. Racing in the rain and with nitrous feels much steadier.
- **No more random zooms during loading screens.** Menus and loading screens are drawn for 4:3 TVs, with black strips at the sides, and the port enlarges them to fill your 16:9 screen. When something briefly reached those strips (the circle animation on loading screens for example), the picture behind it jumped in size for a brief moment. The size stays put now.

releases.body:
**A big speed update for both games on the Switch.** Races, especially in the rain, now run close to the game's own top speed of 30 FPS most of the time. Freezes during races are minimised.

### Features

- Measured in rain races on the Switch (at the default 1x picture size):

  |                                    | v0.4.0                 | v0.5.0   |
  | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------- | -------- |
  | Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition       | 23 frames per second   | **28.5** |
  | Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition Remix | 20.5 frames per second | **27.5** |

  The game itself never runs faster than 30, as on the original Xbox, so most of the time you are now at or near full speed.
- **No more half-second freezes in races.** The game stopped for about half a second now and then during a race, most often right after the start.
- **Sharper look for less effort (Remix).** The Remix's glow and blur effects are drawn at normal size even when you raise the picture size, which cost a lot of speed for something that is blurred anyway.

### Other changes

- Each game now has its own tuned graphics settings, so improving one game does not change the other.

## NeoST 0.6.3 — NetUSBee USB and built-in networking

- **NetUSBee USB devices:** connect a virtual USB keyboard, mouse or disk image
  to either port. Hot-plug devices in Configuration → Network, save them in
  profiles, or use `--usb1` / `--usb2` in the headless runner. USB4TOS drivers

remain external to save states. USB passthrough and isochronous transfers are not
implemented.

releases.name: NeoST 0.6.1
releases.body:
## NeoST 0.6.1 — your settings stay put

A patch release. No new features: **23 defects** found and fixed across five rounds of multi-agent bug hunting, plus a hardware-validation pass on the published packages.

### Settings are saved again

On macOS and on every AppImage, NeoST runs from **read-only media**, so it stores its configuration in your user directory — but it never created that directory, and every setting was silently lost when you closed the emulator. **Five of the eight packages were affected.** Machine profile, video, audio and MIDI setup now survive a restart.

### Also fixed

- **The macOS disk image installs by drag and drop.** It shipped with the app alone, no `Applications` shortcut.
- **The web build ships its licences** (GPL-3.0, GPL-2.0, third-party notices), like every other package.
- **A save-state can no longer be reloaded under a different ROM.** The pairing relied on two bytes of TOS version, which five localisations share, so resuming under the wrong ROM froze the CPU without a word. The state format is now **v19**; v18 and older are refused explicitly, with a message that says why.

releases.body:
**New — Frame Generation (experimental)**
- **Frame Generation ships as an opt-in**: toggle it live in the Quick-Access blade (L3+R3) or per
  game in settings. It runs AMD FidelityFX optical-flow frame interpolation inside Ryudeck's own
  Vulkan present path — no external layers — presenting an interpolated frame between each pair of
  real frames on a dedicated present thread. GPU-light titles roughly double their perceived
  frame rate (measured on device: ~21-30 fps rendered → ~42-60 presented).
- It is self-limiting by design: generation only engages when it actually helps — it suspends below
  a per-title frame-rate floor, when the GPU has no spare headroom (measured from real per-frame GPU
  time, so misreported "100% busy" titles are handled), and when the game already runs near panel
  rate. A zero-delay dip veto skips generation for any single spiked frame (e.g. a shader-compile
  stall), so sudden hitches are never smeared into interpolated frames.
- Fixed: the feature now engages reliably on every launch (previously a first-launch state could
  latch process-wide), the blade reports its live state honestly (including a "restart game" hint

- **Console Mode**: choose Docked or Handheld globally *and* per game, with a live mode tag in the overlay. Your per-game choice always outranks the built-in recommendation.

# Lua Scripting
- Added Lua 5.4 scripting: `File > Script > Lua` opens a script editor on win32, Qt and GTK, with syntax colouring, line numbers, completion, an API reference, a console and session restore.
- Added a script debugger: breakpoints (with conditions, hit counts and log messages), Step Into / Over / Out, Break on Errors, and Variables, Watch, Call Stack and Breakpoints panels.
- 28 example scripts under `Help > Examples`: FPS Counter, Sprite Boxes, RAM Heat Map, Input Display, Cheat Finder, Trace Logger and more.
- `-lua <script>` runs a script from the command line.
- `gui.set_antialias` smooths lines, circles, ellipses and polygons.
- No speed cost while no script is loaded.
- Guide and API reference: [Lua scripting](https://github.com/shanytc/snes9x/blob/master/docs/lua-scripting.md)

# Enhancement Chips (DSP-1/2/3/4, Cx4)
- DSP-1, DSP-1B, DSP-2, DSP-3, DSP-4 and the Cx4 now run as native chips that match their firmware instruction for instruction, with no dump needed.
- Each chip can also run its firmware dump (new BIOS Manager slots), or the old HLE.

# Nintendo Super System
- Added Nintendo Super System arcade support: Z80 supervisor, 
- key chip, on-screen display, three cartridge sockets and the front panel.
- Twelve of the thirteen dumped cartridges run, including HiROM and DSP-1 boards.
- Named the cartridge DIP switches for ActRaiser, The Addams Family, Lethal Weapon and Robocop 3.
- The supervisor's reset silences the APU too, Restart has to be held as on the cabinet, and nocash's test program is accepted as a BIOS.
- The joypad watchdog is off by default. Fixes Lethal Weapon being thrown off the machine.
- Added hotkey tabs
- Load with Preview now shows previews

- Added support for the BIOS in the BIOS Manager.
- Added support for disc insert and eject (eject resets to the home screen), and the disc's name in the window title.

- Color now comes from the cart instead of the stale SGB palette. 
- Pre-palette fallback goes through BGP.
- DMG-compatibility color is routed through BGP/OBP.
- Carts whose SGB detect beats the Color branch get dedicated patches.
- Note: not all games might work out of the box - some issues might occur during game play / boot.

# Super Game Boy
- MLT_REQ is latched in the ICD2 instead of waiting for the BIOS.
- BIOS mode carries its cycle remainder instead of flooring twice, and deducts GB cycle overshoot (fixes audio pacing).
- Packet bits latch on the rising edge, not the falling one.
- MASK_EN honored on the BIOS pane, LCD-off treated as a freeze.
- Boot logo held on displayed content, hidden under the SGB BIOS, and shown only when a boot ROM was actually assigned.
- GBC-only carts are no longer forced out of SGB BIOS mode on the container path.
- Sprite-limit hack offered in SGB BIOS sessions.

releases.body:
- **Fixed: "Security warning" from ColorOS.** On OnePlus and Oppo tablets, 0.5.0 made the system show "an attempt by a malicious app to damage the system has been stopped" a few seconds after Steam started. Nothing was damaged; a change meant to save CPU in Steam triggered the check, and it is gone.

- Helpers 39, Box64 pp13, Mesa Turnip pp10.

releases.name: Pons 0.5.0
releases.body:

- **Less CPU.** Steam and the game talk to each other without going through proot each time: proot stops fell from about 3,750 to 300 per second, and the app uses about 20% less CPU in game. Same 30 fps.
- **Fixed: Android keyboard bar over the game** when a hardware keyboard is connected.
- Helpers 38, Box64 pp13, Mesa Turnip pp10.

# NgpCraft Emulator v3.15 - what's new

This release is mostly about the built-in BIOS, the one the emulator uses when you have no
`bios.bin` (and the one the web player always uses). It now behaves much more like the real
console BIOS. macOS users also get proper app packaging and Finder support.

## Built-in BIOS: much closer to the real one

Many thanks to **Napomex**, who compared our built-in BIOS with the real one game by game and sent
us a detailed report with a fix for each problem. This work started from that report.

We then ran 123 cartridges for one minute each, with button presses, under both the real BIOS and
the built-in one, and compared every frame. About 70% of them now play frame for frame like they
do with the real BIOS, up from about 25%.

- **Fewer crashes.** Puzzle Link, Puzzle Link 2, Magical Drop Pocket and Densha de Go! 2 could
  crash, especially while saving. The built-in BIOS let the game interrupt it in the middle of a

Kiwi360 0.2.0 is the first public release: faster with the bundled driver, image effects, recommended settings per game, and an updater, so later versions are offered in the app. Testers on 0.1.0: install this one by hand once.

**Faster**
- **Zero-copy guest memory now works with custom GPU drivers.** With Lemon-Ade (the default on Snapdragon) the game's memory used to fall back to staging copies; it is shared with the GPU again, as on the system driver.
- **Lemon-Ade v0.0.9 rebuilt** with 16 more Mesa changes, among them an Adreno 830 workaround and shader compiler and occlusion query fixes.

**More stable**
